$note: Register of npm advisories accepted by the web tier's CVE gate
An entry is honoured only while: it names the GHSA id AND the package; its
reason says why the code cannot be exploited HERE; it has not expired; every
copy of the package in package-lock.json is a dev dependency (never shipped);
and the advisory is still reported. The gate checks each of these.
Use it only for an advisory with NO patched release, on a build-time-only
package we cannot drop. Upgrading is always preferred. Widening this file is
a security decision: it belongs in the PR diff, the reviewer checks the
reason, and the expiry is short so the decision is made again.

accepted.reason: ReDoS when picomatch compiles an attacker-chosen glob with repeated single-branch extglobs. picomatch is reached only through vite, vitest and tinyglobby/fdir at build and test time, compiling glob patterns written in our own config (vite.config.ts, vitest include/exclude, Vite's internal file scans); no request, user input or network data ever becomes a pattern, and the package is not in the browser bundle or the Go binary (the gate checks it is dev-only). Every vite and vitest release depends on picomatch directly, the frontend standard requires Vite, and upstream has published no fix: 4.0.7, the latest release, is inside the vulnerable range. Remove this entry in the PR that bumps picomatch once a patched release exists.
